The dialogue script's extent is proved by a partition check - the twenty messages meet end to end across $9639-$9F0F with no gap and nothing over - and each PPU script's extent comes from parsing it with the grammar of the renderer at bank 0 $8495.

$3B.evidence: 4 places, each ending a clause that a following one continues - 'the life-forms; if you need', 'cannot be removed; I think I goofed up'. ASCII $3B is also ';', so nothing is remapped here.

$3C.evidence: 13 places, every one a comma position: 'was our home, but we were', 'If I fail, I would like you', 'NO.1, fire at the gate'. ASCII $3C is '<', so this IS a remap.

$3D.evidence: 6 places, all inside 'life-forms' or 'self-destruct'. ASCII $3D is '='.

$3F.evidence: 3 places, all genuine questions: 'record your progress?', 'Any luck?', 'What are you doing here?'. ASCII $3F is also '?'.

$5B.evidence: 52 places - the most common non-letter in the script. Ends sentences, appears three in a row as an ellipsis in 'reading this...', and sits inside 'No.1' and 'No.4'. ASCII $5B is '['.

$5D.evidence: 2 places, 'Good Luck!' and 'Do not wait here!'. The argument is the CONTRAST with $3F rather than the shape: this script uses $3F at every place a question mark belongs and $5D at the only two places an exclamation mark does, and never the other way round.

$5E.evidence: 12 places, always in pairs, around NAJU and around 'Warp panel'. ASCII $5E is '^'.

$60.evidence: 1 place, 'don't'. ASCII $60 is a backtick, which is close enough to be no evidence either way; the context is the whole argument.

_glyph_caveat: Every glyph above is derived from context. There is no font in this file to check them against: CHR is RAM and no uploader has been found, so no byte of the ROM is a tile yet. CORRECTION, recorded rather than edited away: an earlier entry in annotations/dispatch.json read $5C-$5F as a single 2x2 graphic, on the strength of bank 1 writing $5C $5E to PPU $21AF and $5D $5F to $21CF, one nametable row apart. The dialogue script then showed $5D used as an exclamation mark and $5E as a quote in running English. Both readings cannot be right for one font, and they do not have to be: with CHR RAM the tile at a given index is whatever was last uploaded, so a title screen and a dialogue box can disagree about $5C. Which of the two is happening here is NOT established, and the bank 0 script is a third data point - it uses $5C where a comma belongs ('LONG AGO,AN ALIEN RACE') while the dialogue script uses $3C for the same job.

regions.name: Dialogue message pointer table
regions.description: 21 little-endian pointers, $960F-$9638, into the dialogue script that follows immediately. Read by bank 5 $8476: LDA $0620,X gives an object's message number, ASL A doubles it into Y, and LDA $960F,Y / LDA $9610,Y fetch the two halves - so the base in the operand is this region's own address, which is the strongest statement available that the table starts here. The entry count is bounded by structure, not by the reader: 21 x 2 = 42 bytes ends at $9639, exactly where the first message begins, with nothing over. NOTHING IN THE CODE BOUNDS IT - the index comes from $0620,X, an object field, and no CPY or mask on it has been found. Slots pointing at the same message: $9BC8 is named twice. That is in the data, not a parse error. Every one of the pointers lands on a message head, and the messages partition the block end to end - two statements from two directions, neither derived from the other.
